items.title: The image of a closed nowhere dense subset under a finite morphism is again closed and nowhere dense
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the image of a closed nowhere dense subset under a finite morphism is closed and nowhere dense (statement lines 12499-12504). The counted proof is a reduction chain of moderate length: after closedness and a reduction to an affine base by locality of nowhere density, it uses the auxiliary finite locally free diagram to replace the situation by one where the source is a finite union of closed pieces mapping isomorphically onto the base, handles the case where all traces are nowhere dense by taking a finite union, and rules out the remaining case by a careful argument that produces an open subset of the source contained in the closed subset, contradicting nowhere density (proof lines 12506-12570). It is H2: all steps are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard topological and morphism properties.
